title: Sadhana v. Dakshinanchal Electricity Distribution Corporation Ltd.
coram: Pankaj Mithal, J.; Prakash Padia, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; Executive Engineer to consider and decide the new-connection application under Clauses 4.2 to 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, most expeditiously and if possible within one month.
headnote: On a writ complaining that a new connection for a tailoring shop was not being processed despite deposit of the estimate and an indemnity bond, the Allahabad High Court accepted the licensee's statement that the Executive Engineer would consider the application in accordance with law and disposed of the petition with a direction to decide the grant of connection under Clauses 4.2 to 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, most expeditiously and if possible within one month. Entitlement was not adjudicated.
facts: Sadhana applied to Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. for a new electricity connection for a tailoring shop. She asserted that she had completed all necessary formalities, deposited the estimated amount, and furnished an indemnity bond, yet the application was not being processed. Counsel for the distribution company stated that the Executive Engineer would consider the application in accordance with law within a reasonable time. The Division Bench took up the writ at Allahabad on 29 May 2019.

holding_units.topic: new connection — consider in accordance with Clauses 4.2 to 4.4
holding_units.holding: Where an applicant for a new connection claims to have completed formalities, deposited the estimate and furnished an indemnity bond, and the licensee undertakes that the Executive Engineer will consider the application in accordance with law, the Court may dispose of the writ by directing that officer to consider and decide the grant of connection under Clauses 4.2 to 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, most expeditiously and if possible within one month, without deciding entitlement on merits.

not_decided.point: Whether the petitioner had completed all formalities and was entitled to a new connection on the indemnity bond
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine occupancy, owner consent, or completeness of the application; it only directed consideration under Clauses 4.2 to 4.4.
